cleared.check: Task 2 (L-1170), SLOAD and SSTORE of the gcc 15.2.0 build at the mainnet revision. Monad mainnet runs MONAD_TEN (monad_mainnet.cpp:30-31 of monad v0.16.7; the revision names are in category/vm/evm/monad/revision.h:35-39), so the instances read are sload<MonadTraits<10>> at 0x450670 and sstore<MonadTraits<10>> at 0x451fd0 of monad 0.16.7, extracted from the cycle 27 objdump text with research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-monad-gcc-register-spill.work/scripts/fnaddr.py into research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-monad-gcc-register-spill.work/out/fn, and compared with runtime/storage.cpp:36-121 of the tagged source, the Context layout (runtime/types.hpp:225-245, 53-60) and the evmc fork f6b7c57e host table.
cleared.result: Both follow the source. Keys and values are byte-reversed with vpermq 0x1b and a vpshufb mask whose 32 bytes, read from the ELF at 0x7f52a0, are 07..00 0f..08 07..00 0f..08, which reverses all 32 bytes. sload calls access_storage (host table +0x68) with the recipient at Context+0x28, charges 0x1f40 = 8000 only when the status is 0 (EVMC_ACCESS_COLD), exits OutOfGas (status 3) when gas goes negative, then calls get_storage (+0x08) and stores the reversed word. sstore exits with Error (2) when flag bit 0 (EVMC_STATIC) is set, exits OutOfGas when gas_remaining + remaining_block_base_gas <= 0x898 = 2200, which is the source's test against 2300 with minimum_store_gas 100, charges 8000 on a cold slot, calls set_storage (+0x10) and update_page (+0x80, index 16 of the host table), and charges (first_page_write ? 2800 : 0) + (grew_state ? 17000 : 0). The branch-free form was worked through: sbb gives -1 when first_page_write is 0, masked to -2800; neg and a 32-bit and give 17000 or 0; adding 0xaf0 = 2800 gives the same four values as 100 + 2800a + 17000b - 100 in storage.cpp:91-100. The refund counter is not touched, as in the MIP-8 branch of the source. The MONAD_TEN and MONAD_NEXT instances have identical instruction streams after addresses are removed (research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-monad-gcc-register-spill.work/scripts/normdiff.py: 54 and 76 instructions, 0 differ). These routines serve the interpreter and native code alike, so they cannot make the two engines disagree, and they match the source on what PoolManager storage reads and writes return (src/libraries/Pool.sol, src/libraries/Position.sol, src/libraries/StateLibrary.sol).

cleared.check: Task 2 (L-1170), the keccak wrapper and memory growth of the gcc build: sha3<MonadTraits<10>> at 0x343f90 (and the MONAD_NINE instance at 0x343dc0, identical after rip-relative targets are resolved), Context::increase_capacity at 0x433930, monad_vm_runtime_increase_capacity at 0x4335b0, and the hand-written .increase_capacity trampoline at 0x4334b9 that native code reaches from monad_vm_runtime_increase_memory_raw_mip3. Compared with runtime/keccak.hpp:27-46, runtime/types.hpp:266-356, runtime/context.cpp:46-80 and :151-154, and runtime/context.S:91-175.
cleared.result: All follow the source. sha3 bounds size and offset below 2^28 (high limbs zero and low limb & 0xfffffffff0000000 zero, else OutOfGas), skips memory work for size 0 and hashes zero bytes at offset 0, and for size > 0 grows memory when offset + size exceeds memory.size (Context+0x108). The MIP-3 cost is (min_size + 31) >> 6, which equals ceil(min_size / 32) >> 1 for every input because floor(floor(a/32)/2) = floor(a/64). The new size is (min_size + 31) & ~31, the total bound is data - data_handle + new_size <= 0x800000, the charge is new_cost - memory.cost with the OutOfGas exit, and increase_capacity is called with the old size only when capacity < new size. The word charge is ((size + 31) >> 5) * 6, then monad_keccak256(memory.data + offset, size). monad_vm_runtime_increase_capacity allocates 2 * (parent + new_size) bytes aligned to 32, asserts the allocation, copies the old parent + old_size bytes and zeroes the rest in 32-byte non-temporal stores with the alignment asserts of the source, frees the old handle only when it differs from parent_handle (Context+0x130), and sets capacity, data_handle and data as context.cpp:74-77 do. The trampoline saves ymm0 to ymm4 and rax, r8 to r11 around the gcc call, which together with the SysV callee-saved set covers every register context.S:97-106 declares callee-saved, so a gcc register choice inside the C routine cannot reach native code's live values. The Memory field offsets used (size 0x108, capacity 0x10c, data 0x110, cost 0x118, data_handle 0x120, parent_handle 0x130) follow from runtime/types.hpp:95-117. The PoolManager hashes 64-byte keys and pool keys (src/libraries/Pool.sol, src/libraries/Position.sol:calculatePositionKey, src/types/PoolId.sol) through this path in both engines.

cleared.check: Task 3 (L-1170), gas forwarded by CALL and STATICCALL in native code against the interpreter. research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-monad-gcc-register-spill.work/scripts/gasfwd.py builds one caller and two callees and runs them through the cycle 27 fixed harness (build/0.16.7/hxf, MonadTraits<MONAD_TEN>), which executes each transaction in the interpreter and in native code and compares status, gas left, return data, storage, transient storage, balances and logs. Shapes: CALL(gas(), to, value) as at src/types/Currency.sol:48, CALL(gas(), token, 0) as at src/types/Currency.sol:73 and src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134, STATICCALL(gas(), ...) as in the balanceOf call reached from src/types/Currency.sol:94, and literal gas words 0, 1, 2299, 2300, 2301, 10000, 99999, 100000, 2^63-1, 2^63, 2^64, 2^64+5, 2^255 and 2^256-1 for CALL, STATICCALL and CALL with value. One callee returns GAS at the start of its only block, the other reads GAS in the middle of a longer block, so remaining_block_base_gas is nonzero at the read. The caller stores its own GAS, every success flag and every returned GAS word (182 slots). 160 transaction gas limits: 10 fixed levels from 51,000 to 150,021,000 and 150 drawn with random.Random(29029) between 40,000 and 3,000,000.
cleared.result: 160 of 160 scenarios SAME: in every one the interpreter and native code agree on every stored success flag and forwarded gas word, the gas left and the status (124 runs that succeed and 196 that halt, counted over both engines). The out-of-gas boundary inside the sequence falls between the sampled levels and moves the same way in both engines. This harness is a clang build, so it tests the emitter's GAS and remaining_block_base_gas logic as written in the source and the runtime as built by clang; the gcc runtime routine that both engines of a validator share was read in cycle 28 and is identical at MONAD_TEN (entry above). A gas-sensitive hook or token therefore sees the same forwarded gas in both engines. Raw output: research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-monad-gcc-register-spill.work/out/gasfwd/hx-stdout.txt.

cleared.check: What a wrong register or spill decision of the gcc-built emitter could do to a mined block, and whether mined history already rules it out on the paths it has used. Read cmd/monad/main.cpp at v0.16.7 and monad-eth-block-policy/src/lib.rs at monad-bft v0.16.7, and queried three Monad endpoints on 2026-11-27 (rpc.monad.xyz, rpc1.monad.xyz, rpc-mainnet.monadinfra.com, each answering web3_clientVersion Monad/0.16.7).
cleared.result: A node started with call tracing executes blocks with vm::VM::InterpreterOnly (main.cpp:485-488), and other nodes use Dual mode, which runs hot contracts as gcc-emitted native code. Every node checks that a proposal's delayed execution header (the full EthHeader of block N minus the execution delay, with state root, receipts root, logs bloom and gas used) equals the header its own execution produced, and rejects the block as not coherent otherwise (monad-eth-block-policy lib.rs:1182-1196, 1271-1289). The three endpoints serve debug_traceTransaction with callTracer for a PoolManager swap of block 125,728,461 (tx 0x239f9e91bf990c6a64f6f8a1d4a3d3aa62b0550c2e987a1af9f8eef84fd0f72f; 99,143 bytes of frames, gasUsed 0x1a9b5f on all three), so they run call tracing and therefore the interpreter, and all three return the same hash, state root and receipts root for block 125,729,880 near the head. So for every block these nodes accepted, the interpreter's result equals what producers running gcc native code committed. A gcc register or spill fault on a path that mined transactions use and that changed state, a log or gas used would have split the tracing nodes from the chain. A fault confined to a PoolManager block that no mined transaction has entered is not excluded by this; see the leads.

cleared.check: Task 1 (L-1167), partial reading of the gcc register bookkeeping: Stack::insert_general_reg at 0x3ad250 (76 instructions) against virtual_stack.cpp:769-780 and StackElem::insert_general_reg at virtual_stack.cpp:174-182. Stack::alloc_general_reg (0x3ad770) and Stack::alloc_avx_reg (0x3ad620) were extracted; they construct a new element and call the insert routine, as virtual_stack.cpp:797-811 do.
cleared.result: The control flow matches the source: if the element already holds a general register (the engaged byte of the optional at element+0x57) it returns a reservation with no spill; if the free-register queue is empty (begin and end pointers at Stack+0x70 and +0x78 equal) it calls the spill routine and copies the spilled element's optional StackOffset (element+0x40 to +0x48) into the result; it then takes a register and returns a reservation that increments the element's reference count and reservation count. Field offsets were inferred from the code and the source order, not checked against DWARF. No instruction stream was produced, so this does not show that the native code equals the clang listing.

The other 20 networks run go-ethereum, reth, Nitro, bor, BSC clients, Avalanche's libevm, Tempo, MegaETH, Arc or HyperEVM builds, whose interpreters are covered by Check 4 of OPCODES.md and their own units. leads.question: Which of the PoolManager's 913 compiled blocks have mined Monad transactions entered since validators moved to the gcc 0.16.7 package? Replay the PoolManager frames of mined transactions (call frames from debug_traceTransaction, storage from the parent block) in tools/opdiff/pyevm.py, record the program counters, and map them to the IR blocks of cycles/028/theme-monad-native-unentered-blocks.work/scripts/blocks.py.
leads.why: The consensus check between interpreting tracing nodes and producers covers exactly the blocks mined transactions entered. The complement bounds where a gcc register or spill fault could still be hidden, and it tells the model of the first lead which blocks to run first. Monad endpoints serve only callTracer, so coverage has to come from a replay.

leadResults.answer: The gcc emitter's register, spill and stack offset logic was not run. Stack::insert_general_reg was read and matches the source's control flow. Mined Monad blocks are checked by tracing nodes that run only the interpreter (main.cpp:485-488, block policy lib.rs:1182-1196), and three such endpoints agree at block 125,729,880, so no gcc fault has changed a mined result on the paths mined transactions use. Blocks never entered on mainnet remain uncompared; the model's stopping point is in the leads.

sload, sstore, sha3, Context::increase_capacity, monad_vm_runtime_increase_capacity and the .increase_capacity trampoline of the gcc build match the v0.16.7 source at MONAD_TEN. call_impl, sload and sstore are instruction-identical between MONAD_TEN and MONAD_NEXT, so cycle 28's reading of call, tload and tstore holds at the mainnet revision. Gas forwarded by CALL and STATICCALL with gas() and with 14 literal gas words, with and without value, to callees reading GAS at block start and mid-block, is equal in interpreter and native code at 160 gas limits (seed 29029).
